subtitulo: Moving emphasis without raising your voice
descripcion: English word order is rigid, so shifting emphasis requires structural moves rather than the free reordering Spanish allows. These structures are the clearest single marker separating C1 writing from B2 writing, and the most reliably absent from advanced learners' output.

filas: *Not until / Only after / Rarely / Never / Little* + **aux + subject**
Not until I'd lived there did I understand.
What struck me was the silence.
It was the bureaucracy that broke me.
*All I wanted was…* / *The thing that got me was…*

ejemplos.texto: *Not until I'd lived there a year did I understand why nobody complains.*
*What struck me most wasn't the language — it was the silence on trains.*
*It was the bureaucracy, not the weather, that nearly broke me.*
*All I wanted was somebody to explain the recycling.*
*Little did I know how long the paperwork would take.*

notas: Negative inversion requires auxiliary inversion: *Not only did I…*, never *Not only I did…*.
These structures are marked. Two or three in a text is stylish; six is theatrical.
The *All I wanted was* pattern is the one to start with: informal, frequent, and it teaches the cleft logic without the formal register.

contraste.es: Spanish moves emphasis by moving words (a mí no me gustó). English cannot, so it builds a structure instead. Every Spanish emphatic word-order shift needs a cleft or an inversion in English, not a word-order change.
contraste.de: Because German is verb-second, negative openers are followed by inversion automatically (Nie habe ich so etwas gesehen), which makes Never have I seen… feel natural. The difficulty is do-support: Never thought I is a typical calque of Nie dachte ich. It-clefts are used less in German, so they need deliberate practice.
contraste.it: Italian can focus the subject simply by placing it after the verb (L'ha detto Maria), where English needs a cleft (It was Maria who said it). Italian speakers therefore need clefts more often than they expect; negative inversion with do-support has no Italian model.
contraste.fr: It-clefts are the default emphasis in French (c'est… qui/que), so they come very easily, sometimes too often. Literary French also inverts after openers such as rarement or à peine (Rarement a-t-on vu…), a close model for Rarely have we seen….
contraste.pt: Portuguese focuses through free word order and clefts (foi a Maria que disse), so it-clefts come easily. The pseudo-cleft is especially frequent (o que eu quero é…), which makes what I want is… natural; negative inversion has no Portuguese model.

errores: *Never I have seen* instead of *Never have I seen*.
Using inversion where plain order carries the same weight, so the emphasis reads as unearned.

es: *fue entonces cuando* rendered as *It was then when…* instead of *It was then that…*.
de: Inverting after any fronted adverb, as German V2 requires: *Then have I realised* instead of *Then I realised*.
it: Dropping the dummy subject in a cleft, as in *è Maria che ha deciso*: *Is Maria who decided* instead of *It was Maria who decided*.
fr: Using *it is … that* for every emphasis because *c'est … que* is the default French focus device, producing clefts where stress alone would do.
pt: Dropping the dummy subject in a cleft, as in *é a Maria que decidiu*: *Is Maria who decided* instead of *It was Maria who decided*.

mision.consigna: Write about a moment of culture shock you actually had.
requisitos: no more than six marked structures in total

microtareas.texto: Take five flat sentences about your life abroad and rewrite each as a cleft.
Write three negative inversions. Check the auxiliary every time.
Record 90 seconds about something that surprised you on arrival, using at least two clefts.

autochequeo: Is the auxiliary present in every inversion?
Two different cleft types, or the same one twice?
Does each one earn its emphasis, or is it decoration?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on inversion, clefts and emphatic structures. (1) Check the auxiliary in every inversion. (2) Say whether each structure earns its emphasis or is decorative. (3) Show where plain word order would be better. (4) Give one alternative structure for my three best sentences. Do not rewrite the text.
